title: Great Partnerships Defer to Expertise and Passion
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This Field Note offers three pre-agreed rules for resolving gridlock in strong partnerships: defer to whoever has the deepest expertise, defer to whichever party feels the strongest passion when expertise is roughly equal, and defer the decision altogether if either party genuinely cannot live with the outcome. The key insight is timing -- these rules must be agreed upon before conflict arises, not negotiated in the heat of disagreement. The piece treats the ability to postpone a decision as a legitimate and even necessary tool for preserving a relationship, rather than a failure to resolve the issue.
points: Three deferral rules help resolve gridlock: expertise, passion, and the 'can you live with it' test.
These rules work best when agreed upon at the start of a partnership, before any specific conflict arises.
Deferring to expertise is the first-line rule when one party clearly knows more about the issue.
When expertise is equal, deferring to whichever party feels the issue more passionately is recommended.
Postponing a decision entirely is presented as an acceptable outcome when neither party can accept the result.
quotes: Making decisions together requires working through complex issues and different points of view.
The first rule is to defer to the judgment of the party with deepest expertise on the issue.
The second rule is to defer to the passion and strong sentiment of one of the parties.

If either party finds the outcome so reprehensible, uncomfortable, or distasteful, the parties then simply postpone or shelve the decision altogether to preserve the relationship and to offset future bitterness.
Good relationships deal with the potential potholes in the road long before they start driving.
